title: P03: untied entrance and exit around a shared middle block
description: P03: replace the third logical block with the second block, yielding A-B-B-D while retaining distinct initialized entrance and exit blocks throughout pretraining and downstream RL/evaluation. Reusing only the middle transformation may encourage transferable proof operations without forcing input parsing and output readout to share their parameters.
hypothesis: P01 A-B-A-B sharing in run 014 scored 75.33 versus incumbent 147.67, but shared the entrance and exit operations as well as halving unique capacity. P03 has not been tested: retaining independent entrance and exit blocks while repeating the middle transformation may preserve specialization and improve the starting policy for fixed expert iteration. This reduces unique parameters by one block (789760, about 24.6%) and keeps four logical applications; it does not isolate sharing from capacity reduction or the identity of the retained initialized blocks. Reduced capacity may still harm transfer. Only downstream three-seed dev-transfer performance decides keep/discard.
expected_delta: Central prediction +3 to +15 dev-transfer theorems at true length >=7 versus incumbent 012 (exact mean 147.67; stored rounded mean 148), with plausible downside -75 given P01. Four logical block applications retain approximately the incumbent per-token compute; expect roughly 3000 pretraining steps in 300 seconds, with a modest reduction in optimizer work. Learned generation lengths may affect total runtime under the fixed 1200-second cap.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py), shared middle block A-B-B-D
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: Construct fork GPT with four logical blocks, alias blocks[2] to blocks[1], then load state. Live harness preserves sharing throughout RL; KV caches remain per logical application.

config.init: fork default normal 0.02; construct all four blocks then alias block 2 to block 1; retain original blocks 0,1,3 and unchanged RNG state
